s0004.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongding, on yihai day, the Founder assumed the imperial dignity at the Southern Suburb. With firewood piled for the burnt offering he announced to Heaven: "The Emperor, your subject Baxian, [1] dares to use a black bull to proclaim clearly to the August Empress and August Emperor: The House of Liang, its edifice crumbling, calamity piled upon calamity, its allotted span exhausted—reverently in accord with Heaven's response, the mandate was given to Baxian.
s0004.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongding (557), on yihai day, the Founder took the throne at the Southern Suburb. He kindled the firewood offering and addressed Heaven: "Your subject Baxian, now Emperor, [1] ventures to sacrifice a black bull and declare to the August Empress and August Emperor: The Liang dynasty lies in ruins, disaster heaped upon disaster, its mandate spent—yet Heaven's answer has come, and the charge is laid upon Baxian."

s0005.literal: From the beginning there have been the multitude of people; therefore rulers were set over them, choosing the worthy and able—never always of one surname.
s0005.idiomatic: When the people first arose, rulers were appointed over them; worth and ability, not bloodline alone, decided who would lead.

s0006.literal: In the ages of Fangxun and Chonghua, both were without intent to receive the end; the lords of Dangtu and Dianwu, though they had mind for yielding, all alike placed men of outstanding talent upon the ten-thousand chariots, with high merit steering the four seas—therefore they could greatly shelter the black-haired people and brightly settle the districts and counties.
s0006.idiomatic: Yao and Shun took the throne without seeking it; the rulers of Wei and Jin, though they spoke of abdication, still set men of rare talent upon the throne and men of towering merit at the helm of the realm—thus they sheltered the people and brought order to the land.

s0007.literal: In the final fortune of Liang, misfortune still followed misfortune; savage foes leaned upon the borders, and for long the sacred vessel shifted. Emperor Chengsheng was abroad and could not sacrifice to Xia; Heaven had not yet repented the calamity, and again they suffered bandit invasions. The legitimate heir was deposed and discarded; collateral branches usurped by fraud. Heaven and earth were overturned; statutes and norms were extinguished.
s0007.idiomatic: In Liang's last days disaster followed disaster. Barbarian armies trampled the borders and the imperial regalia passed from hand to hand. Emperor Chengsheng languished in exile, unable to keep the altars of state; Heaven had not yet lifted the scourge, and rebels struck again. The rightful heir was cast aside; kinsmen seized power by deceit. Heaven and earth were overturned; law and order perished.

s0008.literal: Baxian at the first cast aside his sleeve and greatly rescued the crosscurrent; again he raised the righteous army and truly conquered many hardships; deposing a king and establishing an emperor, he truly had merit therein; settling the state and fixing the altars, he exhausted his strength.
s0008.idiomatic: The Founder first flung aside his robe and plunged into the flood to save the realm; again he raised righteous armies and truly cut through countless perils. He deposed one ruler and set up another—merit undeniable—and gave all his strength to secure the nation and its altars.

s0009.literal: This is called modest prosperity; one looks toward the Great Way.
s0009.idiomatic: This was modest order; the Great Way still lay ahead.

s0010.literal: Thereafter clouds and mist showed color; sun and moon presented omens; constellations gathered at the Eastern Well; a dragon appeared in the Qiao region. Removing the old and spreading the new, the dark signs were already manifest; shifting from Yu and serving Xia, and moreover matching the songs of praise, [2] the nine domains and eight wilds alike spread forth sincere petitions; the hundred spirits and assembled sacrifices all had sincere wish.
s0010.idiomatic: Then clouds and mist took auspicious hues; sun and moon showed signs; stars clustered at the Eastern Well; a dragon was seen in Qiao. The old order gave way to the new, and Heaven's signs were plain; as in the transfer from Shun to Yu, the people's acclaim agreed. [2] Within the nine provinces and beyond the eight directions, loyal petitions poured in; every spirit and rite was offered in earnest devotion.

s0011.literal: The Liang Emperor, with lofty yielding, surrendered the myriad states and conferred the great treasure. Baxian, considering himself slight, yielded virtue and would not succeed; even to a third time, his refusal could not obtain consent.
s0011.idiomatic: The Liang emperor abdicated with lofty grace and handed over the great seal. The Founder, judging himself unworthy, declined again and again; a third time he refused, yet consent was denied him.

s0012.literal: All said that the hundred surnames needed a lord and the myriad affairs could not be left vacant; the imperial numen favored the mandate—it could not be modestly refused.
s0012.idiomatic: All agreed that the people needed a ruler and the myriad affairs of state could not stand idle; Heaven's favor rested on him—humility was not permitted.

s0013.literal: In awe of Heaven's majesty, he received the fine fortune; ever mindful of long-held resolve, how could he be without shame in virtue?
s0013.idiomatic: In awe of Heaven's majesty he accepted the glorious mandate; yet remembering his lifelong modesty, how could he be free of shame?

s0014.literal: Reverently selecting the first day, he ascended the altar and received the abdication, announcing his category to the August Lord, to answer the people's heart—forever to preserve our Chen.
s0014.idiomatic: He reverently chose the auspicious day, ascended the altar, and received the abdication, reporting to the Supreme Lord to answer the people's hearts—may Chen endure forever.

s0015.idiomatic: May the bright spirits accept this offering!

s0016.literal: " Earlier there had been miasma and fog; day and night were dim and dark. On this day the atmosphere was clear and calm; those who knew recognized that Heaven's Way was at work.
s0016.idiomatic: " Before this, miasma and fog had shrouded the land in unbroken gloom. On that day the air cleared and grew serene; the discerning knew Heaven's Way was at work.

s0017.literal: When the rites were complete, the imperial carriage returned to the palace and proceeded to the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.
s0017.idiomatic: When the rites were finished, the imperial carriage returned to the palace and halted before the Hall of the Supreme Ultimate.

s0018.literal: An edict said: "The Five Virtues rotate in succession—therefore emperors and kings rule Heaven. The Three Rectifications follow one another—therefore Xia and Yin govern the age. Though colors differed in written edicts and times differed in pattern and substance, yielding and warfare, expeditions and punishments, were used in varying measure; yet to nurture virtue and stir the people, the principle returns to one standard.
s0018.idiomatic: An edict declared: "The Five Virtues succeed one another, and thus emperors and kings hold Heaven's mandate. The Three Rectifications follow in turn, and thus Xia and Yin governed the world. Though ritual color and written style changed with the age, and abdication gave way to conquest as times required, the aim was always one: to nurture virtue and lift up the people."

s0019.literal: We, slight and dim, at the time met with hardship and peril; the state's steps repeatedly met distress; Heaven's cords thrice snapped. Diligently we toiled for our forebears and rescued that crosscurrent, relying on our generals' merit and joining the fierce warriors' strength—once to set the realm right and twice to remake the black-haired people.
s0019.idiomatic: "We, unworthy and obscure, came to power in grievous times. The throne stumbled again and again; Heaven's bonds were thrice severed. We labored for our ancestors' sake to stem the flood, leaning on our commanders' deeds and our warriors' might—once to restore the realm and again to remake the people."

s0020.literal: The House of Liang, its heavenly blessing ended forever, its sequence where it belonged, followed the canon of yielding to the able and gathered the great mandate upon Our person.
s0020.idiomatic: The House of Liang, its heavenly mandate exhausted, its turn complete, followed the ancient canon of yielding to the worthy and laid the great charge upon Our person."

s0021.literal: Looking back on Our slight virtue, Our refusal could not obtain clarity; following Heaven's favor, We bow to match the people's heart, receiving the end from the Culture Ancestor, ascending to offer to the August Lord, continuing the traces of the hundred kings, ruling over the ten thousand realms—like crossing river water, We know not where to ford.
s0021.idiomatic: "Reflecting on Our meager worth, We could not refuse with honor; bowing to Heaven's favor and the people's will, We received the mandate from the culture-ancestor, ascended to worship the Supreme Lord, and took up the hundred kings' legacy to rule the world—like a man fording a river without knowing the far shore."

s0022.literal: The precious enterprise newly founded, the imperial fortune newly renewed—We think to extend gracious favor and spread it over the hundred millions.
s0022.idiomatic: "Our dynasty is newly founded, Our fortune freshly renewed; We mean to spread gracious bounty to the hundred millions."

s0023.literal: Let there be a great amnesty for all under Heaven; change Liang's second year of Taiping to the first year of Yongding.
s0023.idiomatic: Let there be a general amnesty throughout the realm, and let Liang's second year of Taiping be renamed the first year of Yongding."

s0024.literal: Bestow on the people two ranks of nobility; on civil and military officials, two grades.
s0024.idiomatic: Grant the people two ranks of nobility and civil and military officials two grades of promotion."

s0025.literal: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the solitary who cannot support themselves—five hu of grain per person.
s0025.idiomatic: Give five hu of grain to each widower, widow, orphan, or solitary who cannot support himself."

s0026.literal: Overdue rents and old debts—all shall not again be collected.
s0026.idiomatic: Overdue rents and old debts shall not be collected again."

s0027.literal: Those who have violated village pure criticism, corruption, lewdness, or theft—all shall wash away prior entries and be given a fresh start.
s0027.idiomatic: Those guilty of village scandal, corruption, debauchery, or theft shall have prior records erased and begin anew."

s0028.literal: Long-term convicts under edict imprisonment—all are specially pardoned.
s0028.idiomatic: Long-term prisoners held under imperial order are specially pardoned."

s0029.literal: Loss of office and forfeiture of rank, prohibition and deprivation of honors—all follow the old statutes.
s0029.idiomatic: Loss of office, forfeiture of rank, and penalties of disgrace and barred honors shall follow the former statutes."

s0030.literal: " Another edict said: "The Rites set forth Qi and Song; the Odes sing of the two guests—the weight of not treating them as subjects, each generation has honored this.
s0030.idiomatic: A second edict read: "The Rites enshrine the houses of Qi and Song; the Odes praise the two guest-lords—the ancient honor of not treating them as mere subjects, which every age has upheld.

s0031.literal: The House of Liang, reverently in accord with the people's lord, took its model from the past; crossing the river and sinking the jade disk, with lofty yielding it surrendered the myriad states—the thatch tribute conferred should follow the old canon.
s0031.idiomatic: The House of Liang, reverent toward Heaven and the people, took its model from antiquity; crossing the river and casting the jade disk into the stream, it abdicated with lofty grace and surrendered the realm. The tribute of thatch we now confer shall follow the old precedent."

s0032.literal: Let Jiangyin commandery be used to enfeoff the Liang ruler as King of Jiangyin, observing Liang's calendar, with chariots, banners, and dress all according to former standards; palace quarters and stipends shall be maintained with full generous elevation.
s0032.idiomatic: Let Jiangyin commandery support the Liang ruler as King of Jiangyin, keeping Liang's calendar, with chariots, banners, and regalia as before; his palaces and stipends shall be maintained in full honor."

s0033.literal: " Another edict made the Liang Empress Dowager Grand Princess of the State of Jiangyin and the Empress Consort Princess of Jiangyin.
s0033.idiomatic: Another edict named the Liang empress dowager Grand Princess of Jiangyin and the empress consort Princess of Jiangyin.

s0034.literal: Another edict ordered the hundred offices to assume their duties according to rank.
s0034.idiomatic: Another edict ordered all offices to resume their duties according to rank.

s0035.literal: On jingzi day the imperial carriage visited Zhongshan to sacrifice at the temple of Emperor Jiang.
s0035.idiomatic: On jingzi day the emperor visited Zhongshan to sacrifice at the temple of Emperor Jiang.

s0036.literal: On wuyin day the imperial carriage visited the Hualin Park, personally reviewing lawsuits and pardoning prisoners on the spot.
s0036.idiomatic: On wuyin day the emperor went to Hualin Park, personally heard lawsuits, and pardoned prisoners on the spot.

s0037.literal: On jimao day he dispatched great envoys to proclaim comfort to the four quarters and sent down imperial-seal letters instructing the provinces and commanderies, saying: "The four kings changed the age—Shang and Zhou thereby answered Heaven; the Five Victories succeeded one another—Xuan and Xi thereby met their fortune.
s0037.idiomatic: On jimao day he sent great envoys to proclaim comfort to the four quarters, issuing sealed letters of instruction to the provinces and commanderies: "The four kings changed the age—Shang and Zhou thus answered Heaven; the Five Agents succeeded one another—Xuan and Xi thus met their destined turn."

s0038.literal: Liang's virtue was unmade; mourning and disorder piled up for years. The eastern domains collapsed in turmoil; the western capital was swept away.
s0038.idiomatic: Liang's mandate failed; mourning and chaos lasted for years. The east erupted in rebellion; the western capital was overrun."

s0039.literal: Xiao Bo defied the statutes—he was not merely Zhao Lun. Hou Jing reached to Heaven—he surpassed Liu Zai.
s0039.idiomatic: Xiao Bo rebelled against the throne—his crime outdid Zhao Lun's. Hou Jing's outrage touched Heaven—it exceeded Liu Zai's."

s0040.literal: Zhenyang turned traitor and usurped; the bandits' pact linked armies. The lands east of the Yangtze long belonged to the Xianbei; Jinling for long was no longer the land of Liang.
s0040.idiomatic: Zhenyang seized the throne by treachery; rebels joined forces in league. The lands east of the Yangtze fell under Xianbei rule; Jinling for long was no longer Liang's."

s0041.literal: From the age of swirling chaos since primordial mist, [3] before the dragon chart and phoenix record, from the beginning of Eastern Han's Xingping, through Western Jin's Yongjia turmoil—the realm split apart, never as in the Liang dynasty.
s0041.idiomatic: From the age of primordial chaos, [3] before the dragon chart and phoenix annals, from Eastern Han's Xingping through Western Jin's Yongjia disaster—the realm has fractured, but never as ruinously as under Liang."

s0042.literal: We, empty and slight, met with the rising fortune. From old upon taking office We first cleared the Yue regions; Xumen and Langbo—none went unmarched upon. Crossing seas and scaling mountains, wherever We went was pacified.
s0042.idiomatic: "We, unworthy and slight, came to power at a time of renewal. From our first rise we cleared the Yue lands; at Xumen and Langbo we left no foe unbeaten. Crossing seas and climbing mountains, we pacified wherever we marched."

s0043.literal: Braving complaint and wind-blown dust, galloping with the army—we extended Liang's sacrifices six times and cut down powerful bandits tenfold. How could one call it human counsel alone? All was opened by Heaven.
s0043.idiomatic: We braved dust and hardship and drove our armies hard—six times we prolonged Liang's rites, ten times we struck down mighty rebels. This was not human planning alone; Heaven opened the way."

s0044.literal: The House of Liang, its heavenly blessing now changed, its allotted span ended forever—reverently in accord with Tang and Yu, they pushed forth their tripod and jade. We yielded east and west, bowed with joined hands and spoke our plea, avoiding Shun's son on the sunny slope of Mount Ji, seeking Zhibo on the wilds of Cangzhou—but the dukes and ministers pressed urgently; the whole land looked up in alarm. Heaven's mandate could not be delayed; thus We received the fine fortune.
s0044.idiomatic: The House of Liang, its mandate spent, its turn complete—like Tang and Yu they offered up the regalia. We yielded east and west, bowed with joined hands and pleaded our case, hiding like Shun's son on Mount Ji's sunny slope, seeking Zhibo on Cangzhou's wilds—but ministers pressed us and the realm looked up in dread. Heaven's mandate would not wait; thus We received the glorious throne."

s0045.literal: This month on yihai We ascended the rites at the Great Altar, thinking of the transfer
s0045.idiomatic: This month, on yihai, We performed the rites at the Great Altar, mindful of the transfer

s0047.literal: [alternate: tong], [4] yet We have shame in virtue.
s0047.idiomatic: [alternate reading: tong], [4] yet We are ashamed of Our meager worth.

s0048.literal: From the time Liang neared its end, for months the sun stood drought-strong; the fire cycle ended, and autumn rains suddenly fell.
s0048.idiomatic: As Liang neared its end, drought blazed for months; the fire cycle closed, and autumn rains burst forth.

s0049.literal: The next day the rites were completed; the round mound was set overnight. Dust clouds cleared at evening; the stars spread at night.
s0049.idiomatic: On the morrow the rites were complete. The round altar had been prepared overnight; evening dust clouds cleared and the stars shone forth.

s0050.literal: The morning scene showed a doubled sun-disk; it dripped the fat dew of Mount Sanwei. The morning light joined jade disks; it bore five-colored minister-clouds.
s0050.idiomatic: At dawn the sun showed a double halo, dripping the sacred dew of Mount Sanwei; morning light joined like paired jades, trailing five-colored auspicious clouds.

s0051.literal: Looking back on Our slightness, We are the more ashamed of this fine blessing. From cockcrow We strive for greatness; We now think of utmost governance.
s0051.idiomatic: Reflecting on Our slight worth, We are the more ashamed of such blessing. From cockcrow We labor for good government and now ponder how best to rule.

s0052.literal: You, bearing halberds in the border provinces, share in responsibility as Our arms and thighs; with divided tallies as famed administrators, [5] We entrust you with compassionate care for the people.
s0052.idiomatic: You who bear command in the provinces are Our arms and thighs; you who hold the tallies as governors [5] are charged with pity for the people.

s0053.literal: The imperial calendar is newly renewed—think of the people's joy. Deeply seek the people's afflictions; strive for integrity and fairness. Cherish and favor to comfort the orphaned and poor; authority and punishment to restrain the violent and cunning.
s0053.idiomatic: The calendar is newly renewed—share in the people's joy. Probe deeply for their hardships; keep government honest and fair. Show kindness to orphans and the poor; use stern law against the violent and cunning.

s0054.literal: If there are reed-marsh bandits, [6] or offenders against military law, chieftains of mountain valleys who tyrannize in hidden defiles—all are within the general pardon; let all know this.
s0054.idiomatic: Reed-marsh bandits [6] who break martial law, mountain chiefs who lord over hidden passes—all are included in the amnesty; make this known everywhere.

s0055.literal: If any still lose the way, they shall have no pardon.
s0055.idiomatic: Those who still stray from the path shall receive no mercy.

s0056.literal: Now We send envoys to proclaim fully the former intent. Think on good government and answer this empty heart."
s0056.idiomatic: We now send envoys to proclaim Our intent in full. Devise good government and answer Our earnest hope."

s0057.literal: On gengchen day an edict ordered the Buddha's tooth brought forth from the Du family's old residence; the four assemblies were gathered for an unbounded great assembly, and the Founder personally came forth before the palace gate to bow in worship.
s0057.idiomatic: On gengchen day an edict brought the Buddha's tooth forth from the Du family's old residence. The four assemblies were gathered for a boundless great assembly, and the Founder came in person before the palace gate to bow in worship.

s0058.literal: Earlier, Qi former Buddhist superintendent Fazian had obtained it in the Wuchan state; it had long been at Dinglin Upper Monastery. In the last years of Liang's Tianjian era, Shramana Huixing of Sheshan Qingyun Monastery kept it in safekeeping. When Huixing was near death he entrusted it to his younger brother Huizhi. At the end of the Chengsheng era Huizhi secretly sent it to the Founder; only now was it brought forth.
s0058.idiomatic: Long before, Fazian, former Buddhist superintendent of Qi, had obtained it in Wuchan; it had remained at Dinglin Upper Monastery. In the last years of Liang's Tianjian reign the monk Huixing of Qingyun Monastery on She Mountain kept it safe. On his deathbed Huixing entrusted it to his brother Huizhi. At the end of the Chengsheng era Huizhi secretly sent it to the Founder; only now was it displayed.

s0059.literal: On xinsi day the Founder's late father was posthumously honored as Emperor Jing, temple name Taizu;
s0059.idiomatic: On xinsi day the Founder's late father was posthumously honored as Emperor Jing, with temple name Taizu;

s0060.literal: the Founder's late mother Lady Dong as Empress An.
s0060.idiomatic: and the Founder's late mother, Lady Dong, as Empress An.

s0061.literal: The former primary consort, the Qian clan, was given posthumous title Empress Zhao; the heir Ke was titled Filial and Cherishing Crown Prince.
s0061.idiomatic: The former primary consort of the Qian clan was posthumously titled Empress Zhao; the heir Ke was named Filial and Cherishing Crown Prince.

s0062.literal: Lady Zhang was established as Empress.
s0062.idiomatic: Lady Zhang was installed as empress.

s0063.literal: On guiwei day Emperor Jing's tomb was honored as Ruiling and Empress Zhao's tomb as Jialing, following Liang's early garden-tomb precedent.
s0063.idiomatic: On guiwei day Emperor Jing's tomb was styled Ruiling and Empress Zhao's Jialing, following Liang's early garden-tomb precedent.

s0064.literal: Revision and codification officers were established to compile and fix laws and ordinances.
s0064.idiomatic: Officers for revision and codification were appointed to compile laws and ordinances.

s0065.literal: On wuzi day the spirit tablet of Emperor Jing was moved to take its place in the Grand Temple.
s0065.idiomatic: On wuzi day the spirit tablet of Emperor Jing was enshrined in the Grand Temple.

s0066.literal: On xinmao day the Central Authority General, Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, and Danyang Intendant Wang Chong was made Left Grand Master of the Palace.
s0066.idiomatic: On xinmao day Wang Chong, central authority general, grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, and Danyang intendant, was made left grand master of the palace.

s0067.literal: On guisi day the Founder's elder brother, Liang former Scattered Cavalry Palace Attendant, General Who Pacifies the North, and Yanzhou Inspector [7] Duke Daotan of Changcheng county, was posthumously honored as Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Grand Tutor and enfeoffed as King of Shixing;
s0067.idiomatic: On guisi day the Founder's elder brother, the late Liang scattered-cavalry palace attendant, general who pacifies the north, and Yanzhou inspector [7] Duke Daotan of Changcheng county, was posthumously made grand general of agile cavalry and grand tutor and enfeoffed as King of Shixing;

s0068.literal: his younger brother, Liang former Palace Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, and South Xuzhou Inspector Marquis Xiuxian of Wukang county [8] was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Minister of Education and enfeoffed as King of Nankang.
s0068.idiomatic: his younger brother, the late Liang palace attendant, grand general of agile cavalry, and South Xuzhou inspector [8] Marquis Xiuxian of Wukang county, was made grand general of chariots and cavalry and minister of education and enfeoffed as King of Nankang.

s0069.literal: That month, Western Campaign Commander-in-Chief Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu suffered defeat at Yingzhou and were imprisoned by Wang Lin.
s0069.idiomatic: That month the western campaign commander Zhou Wenyü and Hou Andu were defeated at Yingzhou and taken prisoner by Wang Lin.

s0070.literal: In the eleventh month, on jingshen day, an edict said: "The eastern capital's State of Qi honored kinship as worthy; Western Han's Prince of Chengyang combined merit with affection.
s0070.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jingshen day, an edict declared: "The eastern capital honored Qi for kinship and worth together; Western Han's Prince of Chengyang joined merit with family bond."

s0071.literal: Scattered Cavalry Palace Attendant, Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of Kuaiji and ten commanderies' military affairs, General Who Proclaims Martial Valor, and Kuaiji Administrator Marquis Qian of Changcheng county—his learning esteems pure refinement; his spirit and bearing are concentrated and correct. In letters he joins ritual and music; in arms he settles demonic vapors. With heart-strength and stratagems he governs the family and orders the state. Bearing the halberd as defender, within a month he had achievement. Opening those border passes, [9] his merit surpassed Xiao and Kou; reed-marsh bandits returned of themselves to farming; bamboo-grove magnates submitted to Our sound and calendar.
s0071.idiomatic: "Scattered-cavalry palace attendant, bearer of the staff, commander-in-chief of Kuaiji and ten commanderies, general who proclaims martial valor, and Kuaiji administrator Marquis Qian of Changcheng—his learning is pure and refined, his bearing grave and correct. In civil affairs he upholds ritual and music; in war he quells rebellion. With heart and stratagem he has ordered home and state alike. As territorial defender, within a month he brought order. On the frontier passes [9] his merit outdid Xiao Can and Kou Xun; marsh bandits returned to the plow; mountain lords accepted Our calendar."

s0072.literal: We, empty and few, met the rising fortune. Taking up the three-foot [sword] We received guests at the four gates. The royal enterprise was hard and perilous—we rely on this son. Let him receive lofty rank fitting this primary merit.
s0072.idiomatic: "We, unworthy and alone, came to power in a time of renewal. With sword in hand We opened the four gates to talent. The founding of the dynasty was arduous—we lean on this son. Let him receive exalted rank worthy of his foremost merit."

s0073.literal: He may be enfeoffed as King of Linchuan, fief of two thousand households.
s0073.idiomatic: Let him be enfeoffed as King of Linchuan with a fief of two thousand households."

s0074.literal: The elder brother's son, Liang Central Secretariat Gentleman Xu, inherited the enfeoffment as King of Shixing; the younger brother's son, Liang Central Secretariat Gentleman Tanlang, inherited the enfeoffment as King of Nankang—their ritual ranks the same as full kings.
s0074.idiomatic: His nephew Xu, former Liang gentleman of the central secretariat, inherited the enfeoffment as King of Shixing; his younger brother's son Tanlang, former Liang gentleman of the central secretariat, inherited as King of Nankang—their ritual standing equal to that of reigning kings.

s0075.literal: On jihai day sweet dew fell in the pine forest of Zhongshan, filling the cliffs and valleys.
s0075.idiomatic: On jihai day sweet dew fell in the pine forest of Zhongshan until cliffs and valleys were full.

s0076.literal: On gengzi day a monk of Kaishan Monastery gathered it and presented it; an edict ordered it distributed to the ministers.
s0076.idiomatic: On gengzi day a monk of Kaishan Monastery gathered it and presented it; an edict ordered it distributed among the ministers.

s0077.literal: On jingchen day the General Who Pacifies the West and South Yuzhou Inspector Xu Du was made General Who Pacifies the Right and Commander of the Palace Guards.
s0077.idiomatic: On jingchen day Xu Du, general who pacifies the west and South Yuzhou inspector, was made general who pacifies the right and commander of the palace guards.

s0078.literal: On gengshen day a great fire broke out in the capital.
s0078.idiomatic: On gengshen day a great fire broke out in the capital.

s0079.literal: In the twelfth month, on gengchen day, the Empress visited the Grand Temple.
s0079.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on gengchen day, the empress visited the Grand Temple.

s0080.literal: In the second year, spring, first month, on yiwei day, an edict said: "Setting offices and dividing duties follows the weight of affairs; feathered banners and chariots and horses rise and fall with the times. Jin's Five Commandants sounded the reed-whistle to open the road; Han's Nine Ministers had runners call out together as they passed—rites of Yu and Xia, how could they be one standard? Yin simplicity and Zhou pattern surely have no fixed rule.
s0080.idiomatic: In spring of the second year, on yiwei day of the first month, an edict declared: "Offices and duties are weighed by the business at hand; ceremonial escorts rise and fall with the age. Jin's Five Commandants sounded the reed-pipe to clear the road; Han's nine ministers had heralds cry out as they passed—Yu and Xia rites were not one model; Yin austerity and Zhou ornament had no fixed pattern."

s0081.literal: We have received this precious succession, replacing Heaven's work; We keep in mind the official ranks, that they may match the time's core.
s0081.idiomatic: "We have received the sacred succession and take up Heaven's task; We mean to restore official ranks to suit the present need."

s0082.literal: In Liang's Tianjian era, the Left and Right Valiant Cavalry led the Vermilion-Robed Direct Attendants and were both given ceremonial escorts. The North Xuzhou Inspector
s0082.idiomatic: Under Liang's Tianjian reign, the left and right valiant cavalry led the vermilion-robed direct attendants and were both granted ceremonial escorts. The North Xuzhou inspector

s0086.literal: was the first to hold this office.
s0086.idiomatic: was the first to hold this office.

s0087.literal: [10] Disorder and separation for years on end—the court canon did not survive. The young of later generations scarcely heard the old rules.
s0087.idiomatic: [10] Years of chaos have effaced the court's precedents; the young scarcely know the old rules.

s0088.literal: Now abolishing the Left and Right Valiant Cavalry, they should unite civil and military; for civil officials use trusted intimates, for military officials use meritorious ministers. The ceremonial escort granted shall match the crown prince's two guard commanders.
s0088.idiomatic: We now abolish the left and right valiant cavalry and make the post serve both civil and military ranks—civil officials drawn from trusted intimates, military from meritorious commanders—with escorts equal to the crown prince's two guard commanders.

s0089.literal: For other offices as well, the Masters of Writing shall draw up detailed regulations.
s0089.idiomatic: For all other offices the Masters of Writing shall draft detailed regulations."

s0090.literal: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Hou Tian advanced in rank to Minister of Works; Central Authority General, Grand Mentor with the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, and newly appointed Left Grand Master of the Palace Wang Chong became Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.
s0090.idiomatic: Hou Tian, grand general of chariots and cavalry and grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, was promoted to minister of works; Wang Chong, central authority general, grand mentor with staff equal to the three dukes, and newly appointed left grand master of the palace, became junior tutor of the crown prince.

s0091.literal: Left Guard General Xu Shipu became General Who Protects the Army; South Yanzhou Inspector Wu Mingche advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the South; Hengzhou Inspector Ouyang Yi advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the South.
s0091.idiomatic: Xu Shipu, left guard general, became general who protects the army; Wu Mingche, South Yanzhou inspector, was promoted to general who pacifies the south; Ouyang Yi, Hengzhou inspector, was promoted to general who pacifies the south.

s0092.literal: On xinchou day the imperial carriage personally sacrificed at the Southern Suburb.
s0092.idiomatic: On xinchou day the emperor sacrificed in person at the Southern Suburb.

s0093.literal: An edict said: "We received the mandate and rule as lord; the stars have newly shifted. In the first month of auspicious spring the full rites were performed at the Great Altar. The seasonal signs were bright and splendid; the people's lord approved the celebration. We think to make the hundred millions all share in renewal.
s0093.idiomatic: An edict declared: "We received the mandate and now rule the realm; the calendar has newly turned. In the auspicious first month We completed the rites at the Great Altar. The seasons showed bright signs; Heaven and the people rejoiced together. We mean for the hundred millions to share in this renewal."

s0094.literal: Moreover, demonic vapors of former ages still obstruct today; military affairs have not ceased; levies and corvée are all heavy. Affairs could not be otherwise—we have long known the harm below. Speaking of the black-haired people, We cannot forget them even in sleep.
s0094.idiomatic: "Yet the evil vapors of former days still linger; armies have not rested; levies remain heavy. Necessity alone drove this—we have long known the people's hardship. When We think of the common folk, We cannot sleep in peace."

s0095.literal: Crimes, whether light or heavy, already discovered or not yet discovered—before dawn today all are pardoned and removed.
s0095.idiomatic: Crimes light or heavy, discovered or not—before dawn today all are pardoned.

s0096.literal: Western bandits from Wang Lin downward—all are permitted to return from error; nothing shall be questioned.
s0096.idiomatic: Western rebels from Wang Lin downward may return to the fold without question.

s0097.literal: Recently recruited righteous armies, originally intended for the western bandits, should all be dismissed and sent home to their occupations.
s0097.idiomatic: Volunteer armies lately raised against the western foe shall be disbanded and sent home to their fields.

s0098.literal: Military supplies ordered late and not yet delivered—all are halted. Surplus grain levied in the first year—half is remitted.
s0098.idiomatic: Military supplies still undelivered are cancelled; half the surplus grain levied in the first year is forgiven.

s0099.literal: Provinces, commanderies, counties, and garrison troops must not on their own dispatch envoys among the people; they shall strive to preserve generous care.
s0099.idiomatic: Provinces, commanderies, counties, and garrisons must not send agents among the people without authorization; they shall treat the people with care.

s0100.literal: If there is harassment, the law shall be sternly enforced.
s0100.idiomatic: Whoever harasses the people shall be punished under strict law."
